lesson: In append_event, each tenant's seq must be strictly consecutive (last + 1, starting from seq 1 for a new tenant) and raise SequenceGapError on gaps. Accepting gaps or having append_event attempt inline repair/backfill was rejected.
why: Audit entries were missing during reconciliation; append_event must remain a pure guard while repairs are left to a separate backfill job.
quote: each tenant's seq must be exactly last + 1, and a gap has to be rejected loudly at write time - raise SequenceGapError

lesson: In append_event, an event with type == 'compaction' must advance seq by exactly 100, raising SequenceGapError on any other step. Adding a configurable tolerance knob was rejected.
why: The archiver batch size is fixed at 100 with no partial batches, and tolerance knobs eventually get cranked into permitting unwanted gaps.
quote: an event with type 'compaction' must advance the seq by exactly 100, because 100 is the archiver's documented batch size

lesson: In append_event, handling duplicate seq arrivals with in-place overwrites or blanket no-ops was rejected; duplicates must return False if payload_hash matches, but raise SequenceConflictError if payload_hash differs.
why: Overwriting or silently swallowing duplicate mismatches caused primary and replica exports to diverge unnoticed.
quote: Never overwrite the stored event, and never silently swallow the mismatch either - swallowing is how the primary/replica divergence went undetected for a month.

lesson: When append_event rejects a write, the log entry must contain only tenant, seq, and the reason, strictly excluding the event payload.
why: Payloads can contain PII and the audit pipeline outputs directly to the SIEM.
quote: Tenant, seq, and the reason only - payloads can carry PII and the audit pipeline feeds the SIEM, we are not spraying payloads into it.
